pr_title: refactor(core): add single type for injector token
pr_body:
Currently we have a lot of places where we repeat the type `Type<T>|AbstractType<T>|InjectionToken<T>` which makes it cumbersome to add another type or to type something else with the same signature.

These changes add a new type that can be used instead.

Fixes #39792.
pr_comments: To be honest, I am not convinced this is a valuable change.
IMO it's worth having, because it's a safe change that will allow us to avoid having to adjust 20+ places if we have to make a change similar to https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/37958.

You can preview 2daf941 at https://pr41580-2daf941.ngbuilds.io/.
You can preview 7fcc8b9 at https://pr41580-7fcc8b9.ngbuilds.io/.
You can preview 56d8661 at https://pr41580-56d8661.ngbuilds.io/.
You can preview 38d7c4d at https://pr41580-38d7c4d.ngbuilds.io/.

@crisbeto FYI the current target label is "target: minor", so the change will land only in master (which targets first minor after v12, i.e. v12.1.0). I guess we may want to include that into v12 too?  (note to caretaker: this comment is **not** a merge-blocker, we can merge it with the current set of labels and create a followup PR if needed)
Not sure why it was targeting `minor`. Switching it to `rc`.

# 🚀 feature request

### Relevant Package
<!-- Can you pin-point one or more @angular/* packages the are relevant for this feature request? -->
This feature request is for `@angular/core`

### Description

There should be a type alias defined for values that can be used as an "injection token". Today I think that is roughly `Type<T>|AbstractType<T>|InjectionToken<T>`. This type is repeated all over and defining a consistent alias would make it easier to update in the future and simplify code passing tokens around.

Forked from https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/37958


### Describe the solution you'd like

`type ????Token<T> = Type<T>|AbstractType<T>|InjectionToken<T>`

Not really sure on a name

review_comments: I note that in this file their are no `AbstractType`s available. Was that an oversight or can they actually not be used as selectors?
I think it was an oversight, because abstract types should work as keys already.
Can this also be an `AbstractType`? Was the original type incorrect?
Yes, I think that the previous type was just incorrect.
Here we allowed `Type<any>` does changing this to `Type<unknown>` have any impact?
It doesn't have an impact, because it's a private API.
